summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, multiple sclerosis, ulcerative colitis, and asthma was admitted for her fourth cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the infusion well, with no acute complications. Transaminitis recurred and was managed with increased leucovorin. A repeat lumbar puncture was performed due to a lost sample from a prior admission; results are pending. Her chronic right foot pain persisted without a clear cause, and gabapentin was increased to 400 mg three times daily. Oxycodone was also increased for better pain control, and dexamethasone was tapered. She remained stable throughout the admission, with no signs of infection or neurological decline, and was discharged home with outpatient follow-up for lab monitoring and pending CSF results.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Pain in joint, ankle and foot
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
Herpes simplex without mention of complication
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
